clue.text: Where hand is doubly evident can swimmer go in with edge?

indicators.note: to go in is to be put inside something, so two pieces are placed within another

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
a rim is an edge
a tin is a can
the gar or garfish is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a swimmer can enter the water at the pool's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about swimming, but the definition is a piece of furniture: the flat arm of a lecture-hall chair, where your writing hand rests on an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat rest on a chair supports the writing hand, and is also called an arm, so the hand appears twice.

clue.text: Dairy product turning Enigmatist loopy

indicators.note: turning round means the setter's self-reference is read from the back

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself; the setter is me
loopy and mental both mean crazy

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that cheese is driving him round the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often stand for 'me' by their own pseudonym, so the setter's name here is a two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a hard Swiss cheese with holes, a milk-based foodstuff.

clue.text: Disgrace -  as incest is (when one's left in)

indicators.note: something that has left has gone away, so these letters are dropped

blocks.note: incest happens within a family
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A grim aside defining scandal by reference to incest.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FAMILY loses I and L to give INFAMY. 'Left' does double duty: it supplies L and says the letters leave; the final 'in' reminds you that one I, the one in IN, stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is public shame and notoriety, a close synonym for disgrace.

clue.text: 13 21 down's garb belongs to Mrs T in trench village in Cumbria

blocks.note: a leat is an open water channel or trench, especially one feeding a mill
Mrs T, Margaret Thatcher, is referred to as her
Stockings is a small settlement near Warcop in Cumbria, the county of the Lake District

explanation.surface: A frontiersman's outfit turns out to belong to Mrs Thatcher, found in a ditch in a Lake District village.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 21 is NATTY BUMPPO, Cooper's scout. Mrs T was the usual nickname for Margaret Thatcher. 'Garb' looks like part of the wordplay but belongs to the definition, the hero's leggings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooper's hero wears buckskin leggings, which gave him his nickname and the series its name, the Leatherstocking Tales.

clue.text: 13 21down's stroke to prevent fellow coming inside

indicators.note: coming inside means entering, so one piece is placed within the word for prevent

blocks.note: to pat is to stroke gently
to hinder is to prevent or obstruct
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A stroke played to stop someone barging in.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 21 is NATTY BUMPPO, James Fenimore Cooper's frontiersman; 's stands for 'is'. PAT then HINDER with F inside gives PATHFINDER, one of his nicknames and the title of a Cooper novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathfinder is one of the names by which Cooper's scout Natty Bumppo is known in the Leatherstocking novels.

clue.text: See 11
People unmentioned -  up to 8

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 8 down

explanation.surface: Speaking of people nobody has named, and what belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the word is read bottom to top before the answer to 8 down joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Others are the remaining people, the ones not already named.

clue.text: See 4
Footballer reaching sign-on age against comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the last two items are read the other way

blocks.note: the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written
taken as written
V, versus, means against

explanation.surface: A footballer reaching the age at which he can sign on, with a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE V turned round gives VEGA. Ramon Vega was a Swiss defender who played for Tottenham and Celtic around this time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramon Vega was a professional soccer player, a Swiss international centre-back in the 1990s.

clue.text: See 11
20's final cut up top

blocks.note: surface reading: Cooper's last haircut
setter's reading: the final example of a crested hairstyle

explanation.surface: Cooper's last trip to the barber.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is COOPER, James Fenimore Cooper. A Mohican is a haircut with a central crest, so the last such cut is also the title of his best-known novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooper's 1826 novel takes its title from the dying tribe, and a Mohican is a hairstyle, so the final one is a last haircut.

clue.text: She's going to get his one out when the Republic's in

indicators.note: out means removed, so a letter is dropped from the possessive word
in means placed inside, so the country goes into the middle of what remains

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland, with 's added

explanation.surface: A woman about to take a man's share once Ireland is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire is the Irish-language name for the Republic of Ireland. The definition is a whole phrase: she is the one who is going to get the inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: An heiress is a woman due to inherit property, so she is someone going to receive a fortune.

clue.text: 20's pioneer gets deft shove from ferry company?

blocks.note: natty can mean neat and skilful
a bump is a shove
P&O is a British shipping and ferry company

explanation.surface: A pioneer gets a skilful push from a ferry operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is COOPER. P&O is the Peninsular and Oriental line, whose ferries cross the English Channel; the ampersand is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty Bumppo is the frontier scout hero of James Fenimore Cooper's Leatherstocking novels.

clue.text: Swore about terrorists wearing breastplates

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for swore goes around the terrorists

blocks.note: to cuss is to swear
the IRA, Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Someone cursed at armoured terrorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like part of the wordplay, but 'wearing breastplates' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuirass is a piece of armour covering the chest, so cuirassed means wearing that armour.

clue.text: Exchange in M&S caused hell to break loose, leading to this?

definitions.text: Exchange in M&S caused hell to break loose, leading to this?

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap one thing for another, here one of the pair of letters for the other
letters that break loose come apart and can be set down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A row in Marks and Spencer that led to bedlam.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap M for S in 'caused' to get CAUMED; that with HELL is shuffled. M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British department store. Chaud-melle is an old Scots law term for a sudden brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaud-melle is a sudden hot-blooded fight or killing, the sort of brawl that a row breaking loose might cause.

clue.text: 13 21down's heard start of letter to Santa?

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: a letter to Santa would open by addressing the one who drives the sleigh

explanation.surface: A child's letter to Father Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 21 is NATTY BUMPPO and 's means 'is'. Santa drives a sleigh, which makes him a sleigher, so a letter to him begins 'Dear Sleigher'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerslayer is a nickname of Cooper's hunter Natty Bumppo and the title of the novel in which he earns it.

clue.text: 20's a carrier for milk and a mineral without splash

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so only the outermost letters of the next word count

blocks.note: taken as written
a milk float is the British electric van for delivering milk
taken as written
taken as written
the first and last letters of splash
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A milk delivery and some mineral water, but without the splash.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is COOPER. A milk float is a slow British electric delivery van. 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat and Ashore is an 1844 sea novel by James Fenimore Cooper.

clue.text: A man in a man, like 20's Democrat

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one man goes within the other

blocks.note: Eric is a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man inside another man, resembling a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: ERIC goes inside A MAN after the M. 20 is COOPER, whose 1838 essay is The American Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooper's political work is titled The American Democrat, so the adjective describing his Democrat is American.

clue.text: Quick look, when that's finished

blocks.note: once can mean when, as in 'once it's done'
over means finished

explanation.surface: A quick glance, taken when the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something the once-over means inspecting it quickly and casually.

clue.text: Best friend's holding tip in old napkin

indicators.note: holding means grasping inside, so the friend word wraps the tip

blocks.note: mucker is British slang for a close mate
the tip is the end

explanation.surface: A best friend holding the tip of an old napkin.
explanation.walkthrough: Mucker is British slang for a pal; 'tip' looks like the corner of the napkin but is just an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Muckender is an archaic word for a handkerchief or table napkin.

clue.text: I say -  a boxer!

blocks.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
a as in 'ten pence a pound', meaning per

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on spotting a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a much-loved British heavyweight of the 1960s. He is also the theme author's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Cooper was a famous British heavyweight boxing champion who once floored Muhammad Ali.

clue.text: County's 17 dough

blocks.note: first meaning: the short name of Buckinghamshire, an English county
second meaning: 17 is AMERICAN, and American slang for money is dollars

explanation.surface: A county's American money.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire, northwest of London, is commonly shortened in writing and speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucks is the standard abbreviation for Buckinghamshire, and in US slang bucks are dollars, so money.

clue.text: See 13
Revere, the setter does, Elizabeth and her top

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the setter says 'I do'
Liz is short for Elizabeth
the first letter of her

explanation.surface: The setter reveres the Queen and her crown.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolize is to treat someone as an object of worship, a stronger synonym for deep respect.

clue.text: See 4
Draw a doctor's cutting implement first

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so the doctor sits within

blocks.note: a tool is an implement
taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Sketch a doctor's scalpel before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts the implement ahead of 'a' in the order. 'Draw' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a prize lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery with prizes drawn from a revolving drum, so it is a draw.

clue.text: See 4
Garbo's wonderful, though with a twist in the tail

indicators.note: a twist at the tail means the final letters are turned about

blocks.note: great means wonderful

explanation.surface: Praise for the film star, with a hint of a sting at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of GREAT swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta was the first name of the Swedish film actress Greta Garbo.

clue.text: In fate, lovers losing love but having energy well-stored

indicators.note: losing means a piece is dropped from the word for lovers
in means placed inside, so the pair goes within the word for fate

blocks.note: one's lot is one's fate
a pair of lovers is a couple
love is zero in tennis, O
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fated lovers whose love has gone yet who are still energetic and well-off.
explanation.walkthrough: COUPLE minus O is CUPLE, which goes into LOT; E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Locuplete is a rare word meaning richly supplied or wealthy, so amply stocked.
